text:
For urban hotel developments, the lifestyle-brand shortlist typically spans **luxury lifestyle, full-service lifestyle, compact/select-service concepts, and soft-brand collections**. A practical global long list is:

### 1. Luxury and upper-upscale lifestyle

| Operator | Brands commonly considered |
|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **EDITION, W Hotels** |
| **Hyatt** | **Andaz, Thompson Hotels, The Standard, Dream Hotels** |
| **IHG** | **Kimpton, Hotel Indigo** |
| **Accor / Ennismore** | **SO/, Mondrian, SLS, Delano, Morgans Originals, Hyde** |
| **Independent/specialist operators** | **Virgin Hotels, 1 Hotels, Nobu Hotels, Pendry, Proper Hotels** |

These brands generally require prime gateway-city locations, strong food-and-beverage demand, distinctive architecture and sufficient investment to deliver destination public spaces. Marriott explicitly positions EDITION and W as lifestyle-led luxury brands, while Hyatt’s current lifestyle portfolio includes Andaz, Thompson, The Standard and Dream. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/luxury-brands?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Upscale, full-service urban lifestyle

| Operator | Brands commonly considered |
|---|---|
| **Hilton** | **Canopy by Hilton, Tempo by Hilton** |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Centric, JdV by Hyatt, me and all hotels** |
| **IHG** | **Hotel Indigo, Kimpton** |
| **Accor / Ennismore** | **The Hoxton, 25hours Hotels, Mama Shelter, TRIBE** |
| **Radisson Hotel Group** | **Radisson RED, art’otel** |
| **Minor Hotels** | **nhow, Avani** |

This is often the broadest competitive set for mixed-use districts, creative neighborhoods and secondary gateway cities. Hotel Indigo emphasizes neighborhood identity; Radisson RED targets vibrant urban locations; art’otel combines lifestyle hospitality with a signature art concept. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/our-brands/hotel-indigo?utm_source=openai))

### 3. Compact, select-service and “urban micro” lifestyle

| Operator | Brands commonly considered |
|---|---|
| **Marriott** | **Moxy, Aloft, citizenM** |
| **Hilton** | **Motto by Hilton** |
| **Hyatt** | **Caption by Hyatt, The StandardX** |
| **IHG** | **Ruby Hotels** |
| **Accor / Ennismore** | **TRIBE, JO&JOE** |
| **Radisson** | **Prize by Radisson** |
| **Specialist operators** | **YOTEL, Generator, Freehand** |

These concepts are particularly relevant where land and construction costs favor **smaller guestrooms, limited back-of-house space and highly activated lobby/bar areas**. Moxy is positioned as a cost-conscious lifestyle development concept; Motto focuses on efficient rooms in central city locations; Ruby uses a “lean luxury” urban-micro model. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/global-expansion-of-moxy-hotels?utm_source=openai))

### 4. Soft brands and collections

For an existing building, adaptive reuse or a project requiring greater design flexibility, developers frequently consider:

- **Marriott:** Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio, Design Hotels  
- **Hilton:** Curio Collection, Tapestry Collection, Outset Collection  
- **Hyatt:** JdV by Hyatt, The Unbound Collection  
- **IHG:** Vignette Collection  
- **Accor:** MGallery, Handwritten Collection  
- **Radisson:** Radisson Individuals  

These affiliations allow more local identity than a conventional hard brand while providing distribution, loyalty and operating systems. Hilton, for example, positions Curio and Tapestry as flexible frameworks for independently minded hotels. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai))

### Most frequently shortlisted overall

For a typical international urban project, the initial “usual suspects” are often:

**EDITION, W, Andaz, Thompson, The Standard, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo, Canopy, The Hoxton, 25hours, Mama Shelter, Mondrian, Moxy, citizenM, Motto, Ruby and Radisson RED.**

Brand availability still depends heavily on **territorial protection, target room count, market tier, conversion versus new-build economics, F&B potential, operator preference and owner return requirements**. Recent portfolio changes also matter: **The Standard is now within Hyatt, citizenM within Marriott, and Ruby within IHG.** ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/may-5-2025-andazmiamiopening?utm_source=openai))
